nodes.text:
Pneumonia can be caused by a wide variety of viruses, bacteria, and even fungi. Here's an overview:

Viruses:

Common viral causes of pneumonia include:

Influenza (flu viruses)

Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)

SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19 virus)

Human parainfluenza viruses (HPIVs)

Adenoviruses

Human metapneumovirus (hMPV)

Rhinoviruses (common cold viruses)

Varicella-zoster virus (chickenpox)

Measles virus

Cytomegalovirus (CMV) (in immunocompromised individuals)

Bacteria:

Common bacterial causes of pneumonia include:

Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus)

Haemophilus influenzae

Mycoplasma pneumoniae (causes "walking pneumonia")

Chlamydia pneumoniae

Legionella pneumophila (Legionnaires' disease)

Klebsiella pneumoniae

Staphylococcus aureus

Pseudomonas aeruginosa

Escherichia coli

Atypical Bacteria:

These bacteria are classified as "atypical" because they require special growth conditions:

Mycoplasma pneumoniae

Chlamydia pneumoniae

Legionella pneumophila

Fungi (less common but significant in immunocompromised individuals):

Pneumocystis jirovecii (common in HIV/AIDS patients)

Histoplasma capsulatum (found in soil, especially in certain geographic areas)

Cryptococcus neoformans

Coccidioides immitis (valley fever)

Aspergillus species

Blastomyces dermatitidis

Parasites (rare):

Parasitic causes of pneumonia are rare and often seen in individuals with compromised immune systems or in specific geographic regions. Examples include:

Toxoplasma gondii (toxoplasmosis)

Strongyloides stercoralis (strongyloidiasis)

Paragonimus westermani (lung fluke)

Total Count:

There are dozens of pathogens capable of causing pneumonia, and the precise count depends on geographic location, population susceptibility, and diagnostic capabilities. A conservative estimate includes over 30 viral and bacterial pathogens, excluding rare fungi and parasites.
